method: Manual A1 review of every fixture that a checker is expected to ACCEPT, against artifacts/audit/evaluation_rubric.yaml. Negatives (bad_*/leak_*/vague_*/missing_*) were spot-checked; each carries at least one lexical defect named by its filename, so they are provisionally accepted as negatives with the caveat that this corpus, too, is unreviewed by its authors.
headline: No worker fixture corpus may be used as a gold standard. All four flash-11 'good' fixtures declare conclusion.type=theorem for open problems (HF-01) and quantify 'for all data in D_w' while also claiming a genericity exception (HF-06). The flash-11 positive corpus is therefore contaminated with the exact defects the gates are supposed to catch.

findings: HF-01: conclusion.type='theorem' for an open conjecture, with no artifact_refs and no proof; this is conclusion inflation.

HF-06: quantifiers.forall says 'for all ... data sets in D_w' while genericity.kind claims an 'open dense subset' with no exception set excluded; the statement then asserts the conclusion 'for all data in D_w', which is the non-generic form.
HF-04: 'forall' quantifier leaves 'complete future null infinity' inside an 'exists' slot, so completeness is not actually asserted of the development in the formal statement.
HF-01: conclusion.type='theorem' for the open C2 SCC conjecture.
HF-06: same forall-/genericity-exception mismatch as the WCC fixture.

HF-06: 'exists: there exists a maximal development that admits no C^2 extension' is an existential quantifier used for what must be a universal conclusion; as written it is satisfied by any single inextendible datum and does not state SCC.
HF-01: conclusion.type='theorem' for the open C0 SCC conjecture.
HF-06: inextendibility statement requires the extension to be 'solving the vacuum equations', which is undefined for a merely continuous metric; the extension class is not well-posed as written.
HF-06: forall-/genericity-exception mismatch as above.
HF-01: conclusion.type='theorem' for the open spherically symmetric scalar-field WCC problem.
HF-06: forall-/genericity-exception mismatch; conclusion asserts 'for all data in D_w'.
HF-04: 'complete future null infinity' appears only inside the 'exists' quantifier, not in the conclusion.
HF-06: formal_statement quantifies 'for all initial data in DataClass' with no genericity exception, while the conclusion says 'For generic vacuum asymptotically flat initial data'; the two disagree.

HF-06: visibility predicate is stated for arbitrary future-directed causal curves from the singular boundary, while the singularity_definition uses incomplete causal geodesics; curve-visible and geodesic-visible singularities differ, so the definition is not well-posed as a WCC predicate.

HF-06: genericity excludes data with 'a trapped surface on the initial slice'; trapped-surface data are the black-hole-forming regime of the conjecture, so this exclusion removes the intended content unless a source says otherwise.
HF-04: sobolev_index=4, weight delta=0.5 asserted without a source; L1 must bind these or the field must be marked unresolved.
POSITIVE: the document explicitly disclaims being a claim (fixture=true, not_a_claim) and uses conclusion_type=open_problem; this is the best-calibrated fixture in the corpus.
SCC content paraphrased to evade lexical tokens; any checker that accepts it has a measured escape. Not a positive example.
All sections present but content tautological; presence checks cannot detect vacuity. Not a positive example.
SCC content in an unrecognised field outside the scanned sections. Not a positive example.
Rephrased leak documented as a known blind spot by flash-13; not a positive example.

Provisional: each negative names a specific defect and spot-checks (bad_01 missing class_id, bad_02 unknown class, bad_03 C0-or-C2, bad_09 bad conclusion type, bad_10 WCC concludes inextendibility, bad_12 vacuum with scalar matter, bad_15 empty, bad_16 garbage; f13 conclusion_inflation, leak_scc_c2, leak_scalar_sph, missing_falsifier, vague_data_class, vague_quantifiers) confirm the named defect is present.
CAVEAT: all flash-11 fixtures, including negatives, also carry conclusion.type='theorem' (HF-01), so the corpus conflates several HF classes; recall measured on it is not per-HF recall.
